help.title: Help
help.tracker_tagline: Defects, Site and FM Issues Tracker (incl. Renovation)
help.setup_1: 1. Sign up and create your company.
help.setup_2: 2. Tap ⚙ Settings — follow the progress badge to configure Projects, Team, AI, Telegram, and Storage.
help.setup_3: 3. Choose your language from Settings → Language (23 languages available).
help.setup_4: 4. Invite your team via Settings → Team (Admin only).
help.setup_5: 5. Create or select a project, then start logging entries.
help.nav_log_desc: Create a new entry — defect, issue, work order, observation, or update — with photos, voice input, and AI-assisted filling. Choose from 8 work categories. The selected category steers the AI to ask for the right domain fields (e.g. CONQUAS assessment zone, Construction Site hazard category, Facilities Management service category).
help.nav_tag_desc: Upload floor plans, pin issues on drawings, compare PDF revisions, and annotate with markup + photo overlays. Works for defects, FM rounds, and renovation punch lists.
help.nav_review_desc: Browse, search, filter, and batch-update entries. AI natural-language search, verification photos, before/after slider.
help.nav_report_desc: Landing overview (status counts, critical alerts, severity chart), section-aware tally, filtered stats, Quality Check NC rate (CONQUAS), Requirements Advisor with reference-document picker, email reports, CSV/PDF/Google Sheets export, AI Query bar.
help.log_1: 1. Pick a work category that fits your site — Building Defects (Landed or Highrise), Construction Site, Interior Works / Renovation, Facilities Management, Infrastructure Works, CONQUAS, or Others. Each category routes the AI to ask for category-specific fields the photo needs (e.g. CONQUAS adds Assessment Zone; Construction Site adds Hazard Category; Facilities Management adds Service Category).
help.log_2: 2. Choose an entry type such as Defect, Observation, Instruction, Work Order, or Update.
help.log_3: 3. Add or capture photos on site. A description OR a photo is enough to submit.
help.log_4: 4. When AI is configured, analysis runs automatically as soon as a photo is captured and the entry auto-saves once AI returns a title or description — no ANALYZE tap, no SAVE tap. A 5-second UNDO / EDIT toast lets you jump back to rectify. Manually-typed fields are preserved; blurry or test shots can still be edited or archived later.
help.log_5: 5. Select component (158 options) and issue (296 options) from the translated dropdown lists — covers building, MEP, finishes, FM, and renovation items.
help.log_6: 6. Fill in location (Level > Zone > Room > Grid), cost, and time tracking.
help.log_7: 7. For one-at-a-time capture, just aim and shoot — the zero-tap flow does the rest. For bulk import (e.g. a folder of photos from yesterday's walk), tap PICK FOLDER OR MULTIPLE PHOTOS below the camera button — each selected image fans out into its own defect record, a BATCH — k of N progress pill shows AI pre-filling the queue, and a staging grid with date filters appears when the selection is large so you can tick only the relevant subset.
help.tag_compare_desc: Open the Tag tab to upload floor plans (JPG, PNG, WEBP, TIF, PDF). Place pins on plans, create entries directly from a drawing, use the heatmap to spot problem areas, and compare PDF revisions with added/removed line detection. Useful for defect walks, FM inspections, and renovation snagging. Overlay site photos onto comparisons with full markup tools (freehand, arrow, circle, text, select/move/delete). Multi-select markups via shift-click (desktop), drag-rectangle marquee, or ➕ MULTI toggle (mobile) — then drag the group, or batch-delete.
help.top_project_desc: Switch between projects or create a new one.
help.top_settings_desc: All one-time setup: Projects, Team, AI, Telegram, Storage, Language. Shows progress badge (e.g. 3/4).
help.top_avatar_desc: Profile, Admin Analytics (admin), Help / Functions / Disclaimer, Feedback, Sign Out.
help.top_ai_query_desc: Shown on Dashboard and Report. Ask questions like 'show critical plumbing in Block A'.
help.set_projects_desc: Create, switch, archive, or restore projects.
help.set_team_desc: Invite members (link + code), assign roles, remove members.
help.set_ai_desc: Connect Gemini (free), Ollama (local), or OpenAI/GPT for photo analysis and search.
help.set_telegram_desc: Real-time alerts to your team group when items are logged or updated.
help.set_email_desc: SMTP for report emails — set recipients, sender name, and SMTP credentials so the REPORT tab can email site reports.
help.set_storage_desc: Choose PocketBase (default), local path, or Google Drive.
help.set_language_desc: Pick from 23 languages. All UI labels, dropdowns, and reports are translated.
help.tip_multi_projects_desc: Use the project selector to switch between sites, buildings, or renovation jobs.
help.tip_export_desc: Report tab: CSV, PDF (on-site fast / office lossless A1 vector), Google Sheets, or all-in-one. Choose which sections to include: Defect Entries, PDF Drawings (pins / notes / markup burned in), Saved Comparisons, and Map (per-entry map thumbnails + consolidated ALL PINS ON MAP page, tile-stitched from OpenStreetMap — no API key needed). The 🌐 EXPORT LANGUAGE selector at the top of the menu defaults to English (Singapore official) and can be switched to a worker's language for native-tongue briefings.
help.tip_data_schema: Open data schema in every Photo ZIP
help.tip_data_schema_desc: The Photo ZIP now ships a versioned, open JSON Schema (schema.json + schema.variant.json when a domain variant applies) that describes every column of the workbook. Each row is also emitted as an _entries.jsonl line — one self-validating record per line, native ingest format for AI / ACC pipelines, BigQuery / Snowflake / Databricks, audit log stacks. The Manifest sheet of _manifest.xlsx points to the schema URI (https://siteshrimp.org/schema/entries/v1.json) so consumers can validate exports without bespoke parsers. Schema is authored open (ISO/IEC standards alignment in mind) and version-stamped so downstream tooling can pin and migrate cleanly.
help.tip_advisor_desc: From the REPORT tab, tap ADVISOR to get AI-powered defect-to-requirement mapping across customised requirements you bring per project (employer's requirements, scope of work, in-house QA standards, contract terms — FIDIC / SIA / REDAS / bespoke developer terms / etc.) plus a small set of industry-recognised standards based on publicly available requirements shipped as references (such as CONQUAS, Good Industry Practice trade guides, Quality Mark, PSSCOC, BTO handover checklist) — useful for defect claims, FM SLAs, DLP disputes, and quality-check sign-offs.
help.tip_language_desc: Switch language anytime from Settings → Language. All dropdowns (components, issues, levels, costs) are translated.
help.tip_batch_update_desc: In Review, tap ✓ SELECT to pick multiple entries, then update status, severity, assignee, or duration in one go.
help.tip_drawing_gestures_desc: Pinch with two fingers to zoom and pan anywhere on a drawing — it now works even while you are marking up. The + / − buttons zoom toward the middle of your view.
help.tip_photo_scale_desc: After placing a photo on a drawing, tap to select it and use the purple − / + buttons in the markup toolbar to resize. You can also drag the corner handle.
help.tip_marquee_select_desc: In drawing markup mode, tap the Select tool then drag on empty canvas area to draw a selection rectangle — every stroke, text, stamp, or photo whose shape overlaps the rectangle is added to your selection. This is the fastest way to pick a cluster of markups to move or delete together. Same gesture works on both mobile (finger drag) and desktop (mouse drag). Shift + drag extends the selection instead of replacing it.
help.tip_multi_select_mobile_desc: With Select tool active, tap the ➕ MULTI button in the markup toolbar to turn on additive mode — each subsequent tap adds or removes an item from the selection (no shift key needed). Tap the button again to return to normal single-tap mode. On desktop, shift / ctrl / cmd + click does the same thing.
help.tip_group_move_delete: Move or delete a group together
help.tip_group_move_delete_desc: Once two or more markups are selected (by marquee, shift-click, or ➕ MULTI), drag any of them to move the whole group together, or tap 🗑 DELETE (N) in the toolbar to remove them all at once. On desktop you can also press the DELETE key; press ESC to clear the selection.
help.tip_markup_autosave_desc: Every stroke, pin, and note you add in markup mode saves automatically — no SAVE button required. The toolbar shows "✓ Auto-saved · N items" so you can confirm your work is safe. Tap ✓ DONE to exit markup mode when finished (work persists). Your markups stay on the drawing when you reopen it later.
help.tip_export_language_desc: REPORT → EXPORT opens a dropdown with a 🌐 EXPORT LANGUAGE selector at the top. English is the default because Singapore's official project reports go to client / architect / QS / main contractor in English. For worker briefings (workers from China, Malaysia, Vietnam, Myanmar, Thailand, Indonesia, Philippines, India and beyond), switch the dropdown to their native language and re-export — the same defect list renders with component/issue/trade/duration/cost values translated. The app UI language (Settings → Language) stays independent of the export — log in your language, export in theirs.
help.tip_photo_filenames: Photos named by project, date, user, defect
help.tip_photo_filenames_desc: Photos uploaded to Google Drive are named Project_YYYYMMDD-HHMMSS_User_DEF-NNNN_N.jpg so you can sort and find them without opening the app — e.g. MyProject_20260416-113200_KH_DEF-0042_1.jpg. Useful for DLP claim evidence, project file organisation, and sharing a photo bundle with the main contractor.
help.tip_map_multi_select_desc: All past and newly added pins stay visible on the map — they persist as database records until you remove them. To work with several pins at once, shift-click (desktop) or tap the ➕ MULTI button (mobile) in the Tag-on-Map toolbar, then tap each pin to add it to the selection (a dashed indigo ring appears around selected pins). Use 🗑 UNPIN (N) to clear GPS from all selected entries at once — the entries themselves stay, only the map pins are removed. Tap ✕ to cancel selection. Individual pin remove (via the popup REMOVE PIN button) still works for single-pin cases.
help.tip_ai_language: AI auto-fill writes in your language
help.tip_ai_language_desc: When AI photo analysis is configured (Settings → AI Setup), the suggested title and description come back in your current UI language. Severity (Critical / Major / Minor / Observation) and Trade values stay in English so search, filtering, and batch operations remain consistent across team members using different languages. Switch your UI language in Settings → Language and the next AI analysis will use the new language automatically.
help.tip_ai_variant: AI churns different fields per work category
help.tip_ai_variant_desc: The work category you pick at LOG steers the AI to ask for the right domain-specific fields, not just the generic ones. CONQUAS projects get Assessment Zone (Architectural / Structural / M&E). Construction Site projects get Hazard Category and PPE compliance, with severity reinterpreted as injury risk (Critical = serious-injury, Major = lost-time, Minor = first-aid, Observation = near-miss). Building Defects (Highrise) gets Block / Tower, Unit, Vertical Zone. Facilities Management gets Service Category and Maintenance Type. Infrastructure gets Asset Class and Chainage. Each variant ships a JSON Schema URI, so downstream AI / ACC / audit pipelines can validate every row against the right contract for that category.
help.tip_ai_provenance: AI output governance — confidence, model, prompt version, human review
help.tip_ai_provenance_desc: Every AI-prefilled defect row carries provenance metadata so downstream pipelines can govern AI output: ai_confidence (0.0–1.0, the AI's own self-rating per row), ai_model (which provider answered: gemini / openai / ollama), ai_prompt_version (semver tag — bumped when the prompt changes), and human_reviewed (flips to true the moment any AI-filled field is edited). field_provenance carries a per-field source map (ai vs human). Use these to threshold rows for auto-accept vs human-review queues, correlate quality drift with prompt edits, and prove which evidence was AI-only versus human-validated for DLP claims and compliance audits.
help.set_maps_desc: Add a Google Maps API key to enable GPS location pinning on entries.
help.tip_map_tagging_desc: When logging an entry, tap TAG ON MAP to drop a GPS pin at the exact defect location (works on OpenStreetMap free or Google Maps). Saved coordinates appear in the entry detail, on the consolidated REVIEW map, and are embedded in PDF reports — each entry gets a per-entry map thumbnail, and a single ALL PINS ON MAP page shows every pin at once with numbered severity markers.
help.tip_map_markup_desc: In TAG → Tag on Map, tap ✏ MARKUP to draw directly on the map. Tools: Zone (rectangle), Radius (circle), Path (polyline), Arrow, Dimension (auto-labelled distance), Stamp (APPROVED / REJECTED / custom), Label, Freehand, and Photo overlay. All markups are anchored in GPS coordinates, move by dragging the coloured handle, and save per project. Works on both OpenStreetMap (free, no key) and Google Maps.
help.tip_convert_desc: TAG → Convert lets you turn photo sketches (pen-on-paper floor plans, hand markups, whiteboard notes) into true vector PDFs usable as Compare base drawings. Pick one JPG or many (batch). Each image is thresholded, traced into SVG paths, and saved as a new drawing record on the backend. Works best on clean black lines on white paper — even lighting, minimal shadow. The converted PDF shows up immediately in the drawings list and is ready for Compare, Tag, and Export.
help.tip_save_device: Save exported files to your device
help.tip_save_device_desc: Tap Dn (Download) on any drawing row to save a local copy. On Android and the installed SiteShrimp app it lands in your phone's Downloads folder (Files → Downloads). On desktop browsers it goes to the system Downloads directory. To reuse a downloaded PDF later for Compare, just tap Up in TAG and pick it from the file picker — it becomes a new drawing record, pickable in the Diff menu alongside any other drawing.
help.tip_load_samples_desc: On an empty TAG drawings list, tap ↓ Load sample drawings to pull two CC0 vector plans (SampleHouse V1/V2) plus two public-domain Dyckman House floor-plan sketches (HABS, Library of Congress) straight from the SiteShrimp samples repo. Use them to try Compare end-to-end without needing your own drawings. Full source / licence notes are in sample_drwgs/ATTRIBUTION.md.
help.tip_cluster_pins_desc: In TAG → Tag on Map, pins added at the same location collapse into a numbered bubble instead of stacking invisibly. Bubble colour reflects the most severe entry underneath (Critical → Major → Minor → Trivial). Tap or zoom in to expand the cluster and reveal each individual pin; drag, popup, and unpin still work on every pin.
help.tip_bulk_delete_desc: Admins can delete many entries at once from two places. DASHBOARD → tap SELECT on the Recent Entries list → pick rows → 🗑 DELETE. REVIEW → tap SELECT → pick rows → 🗑 DELETE in the floating bar. Each action also removes the entry's drawing pins so no orphans remain, and always confirms before deleting — actions are irreversible.
help.tip_advisor_upload_desc: REPORT → Requirements Advisor accepts project-specific PDFs (employer’s requirements, scope-of-work, local standard contracts, bespoke terms). Tap + ADD PDF inside the advisor card, pick one or many PDFs, and their text is extracted in your browser and merged with bundled reference samples (such as PSSCOC, CONQUAS, GIP, HDB BTO checklist) when the advisor runs. Bundled references are publicly available materials from public-sector sources, included as illustrative samples only — copyright remains with each respective publisher; bundling does not grant any licence and does not constitute endorsement. Other standard contracts (FIDIC, JCT, AIA, NEC, REDAS, SIA, ConsensusDocs, local bespoke terms, etc.) are licensed — users hold their own copy and upload it here when needed. Uploads stay per-project in this browser only; the raw PDF never leaves your device, only the extracted text is sent to the AI provider you configured. Remove a document any time with the ✕ next to its name.
help.tip_zero_tap_desc: When AI is configured, capturing a photo triggers analysis automatically — no ANALYZE tap — and the entry auto-saves as soon as AI returns a title or description. No SAVE tap either. A 5-second UNDO / EDIT toast lets you jump to the just-saved record for rectification; tap EDIT to open Entry Detail instantly. Manually-typed fields are preserved (AI won't overwrite what you typed). Blurry or test shots can still be edited or archived later. This cuts per-photo taps from two down to zero on site — the single biggest throughput improvement for walking an entire floor of defects.
help.tip_batch_capture: Batch capture — N photos become N records
help.tip_batch_capture_desc: Below TAKE PHOTO (when AI is configured), PICK FOLDER OR MULTIPLE PHOTOS opens a folder picker on laptop (Chrome / Edge / Firefox) or a folder / gallery picker on Android; iOS falls back to multi-select photo picker. Each selected image becomes its own defect record — not one record with N photos. A BATCH — k of N progress pill above the capture button shows AI working through the queue; you can pocket the phone, switch tabs, or walk on, and records stream into ENTRIES as AI completes each one. A single BATCH COMPLETE — N saved toast fires when the queue drains. Small selections (five or fewer) skip the staging step and go straight into the batch.
help.tip_staging_desc: When a folder or multi-pick returns more than a handful of images (phone DCIM can hold thousands), a full-screen staging grid appears before any AI runs. Thumbnails render via cheap blob URLs so displaying 1 000+ thumbs doesn't spike memory. Use the ALL / TODAY / LAST 7 DAYS / LAST 30 DAYS filter chips plus SELECT ALL / NONE to narrow down, then tap each thumb to tick or untick individually. PROCESS N WITH AI commits only the selected subset to the batch flow. Prevents the 'phone gallery has 2 000 photos' trap from turning into an accidental 2 000-AI-call batch that would torch your daily quota.
help.tip_reanalyze_ai_desc: In REVIEW → ENTRIES, tap ✓ SELECT to enter selection mode, tick multiple entries, then open UPDATE ENTRIES. An AI ACTIONS section appears (only when AI is configured) with RE-ANALYZE N WITH AI. It re-runs photo analysis per entry and refreshes title, description, severity, trade, and component; location, assignee, due date, and status are preserved so your on-site fieldwork isn't overwritten. Useful when entries were logged before AI was set up, when AI improved after the original capture, or when a batch of records needs a fresh pass. Cached photos skip the API (no quota burn); remote-URL photos stored on the backend are fetched and encoded on the fly. Partial failures don't halt the batch — one end-of-run alert reports the totals.
help.tip_undo_edit_desc: After every auto-save the app shows a fixed-bottom pill: ✓ SAVED with the just-assigned title, plus an EDIT shortcut that jumps directly to Entry Detail for rectification — no need to navigate REVIEW → ENTRIES → search. Auto-clears after 5 seconds, or tap × to dismiss earlier. During an active batch, per-photo toasts are suppressed (to avoid N overlapping pills) and replaced with a single BATCH COMPLETE — N photos saved toast when the queue drains.
help.tip_advisor_offline_desc: The Requirements Advisor's reference corpus (PSSCOC, CONQUAS, GIP trade guides, HDB BTO checklist, Quality Mark) is pre-cached by the service worker during install, so the picker works offline on flaky site connections after the first online load. If the library can't be reached, a red REFERENCE LIBRARY UNAVAILABLE strip appears at the top of the Advisor card with a RETRY button — no silent fallback to 'general knowledge'. Selected references that fail to load mid-run are named explicitly in the progress log. When some references fail but others succeed, a PARTIAL ANALYSIS banner above the advisory output lists the missing documents, and the same INCIDENT notice is embedded into contractSummary so the partial-load warning travels with the exported PDF and email. AI call errors (HTTP status, quota, MAX_TOKENS, safety-block, CORS) now surface verbatim in the error bar instead of a generic 'Check AI Setup' message.
help.workflow_quick_desc: LOG → take photo → AI fills title, severity, trade, component → save. Zero-tap auto-save kicks in after your first 10 saves.
help.workflow_batch_desc: LOG → pick folder or many photos → AI pre-fills the queue in the background → keep walking. Each photo becomes its own entry, ISO 19650-named and CONQUAS-bucketed automatically.
help.workflow_conquas_desc: TAG → CONQUAS wizard → pick element (Floor / Wall / Ceiling / Door / Window / Component / M&E Fittings) → 1 photo → AI verdicts every checkpoint. Fails save as linked defects in one batch.
help.workflow_triage_desc: REVIEW > ENTRIES → filter / search → batch-select → set status / assignee / severity / due date in one tap. Batch RE-ANALYZE WITH AI refreshes title / severity / trade across many entries.
help.workflow_overdue_desc: REVIEW > ENTRIES → filter by Open + past due date → bulk comment + reassign. Telegram notifies the contractor automatically.
help.workflow_verify_desc: Open the entry → before/after photo slider → mark Verified, then Closed (Admin only). Audit trail and ISO 19650 filename stay anchored to the original capture.
help.workflow_export: Export & handoff (end of week / project sign-off)
help.workflow_export_desc: REPORT → CSV / PDF / Photo ZIP / Email / Sheets. The Photo ZIP groups photos into folders by your chosen scheme (CONQUAS IF / Severity / Status / Trade / Component / Area), names every file per ISO 19650, and ships a _manifest.xlsx (Manifest + Entries sheets, with the work-category-specific columns), an _entries.jsonl for AI / ACC pipelines, and the JSON Schema (schema.json plus schema.variant.json when a CONQUAS or other domain variant applies). Reviewer-ready for QP handover; pipeline-ready for downstream automated compliance checks.
help.workflow_offline_desc: Captures keep working with no signal — entries queue in IndexedDB and auto-sync when you're back online. Watch the queue badge in the header.
help.purpose_origin_body: SiteShrimp is built by a non-engineer working with AI as a daily thinking partner — a personal learning project that also has to stand up on a real construction site. It is both a daring test of what AI-assisted development can produce when the bar is a court-defensible defect record (not a demo), and a glimpse of what becomes possible when ordinary professionals stop waiting for a tech team and build the tools their own work needs.

about.title: About
about.problem_body:
Construction records are fragmented across photos, messages, spreadsheets, and paper notes. When defects are disputed months later, "I sent you the photo" rarely holds up.

Commercial tools digitise forms but do not solve evidence fragmentation. Site teams still rely on disconnected workflows, inconsistent records, shifting contract terminology, and unreliable site connectivity. Foreign-worker crews often struggle with language-heavy systems, and critical information ends up scattered across tools that do not align.
about.what_body:
SiteShrimp creates a single, structured evidence trail from the point of capture — one capture, one record, one source of truth.

Inspectors take a photo and generate a defect record with AI-assisted fields such as description, severity, trade, component, and location. Each record includes a SHA-256 photo hash, timestamp, timezone, GPS (when available), source type, and change history, with outputs aligned to ISO 19650 naming conventions.

The system is built for real site conditions:
• Phone-first, one-handed use (including with gloves)
• Offline capture with sync on reconnect
• Support for 23 languages
• Flexible workflows: review-first, assisted, or zero-tap
• Free text or dropdown fields with configurable entry types

Drawings and visuals are integrated into the same record:
• Pin defects directly on PDFs
• Mark up photos
• Compare drawing revisions with AI-assisted summaries

Reports are generated directly from structured data:
• PDF reports with sign-off blocks
• CSV exports
• Email summaries (multi-language)
• Google Sheets integration
• ZIP photo packs named to ISO 19650

A recoverable archive supports soft delete, and status updates can trigger chat-based notifications.
about.requirements_body:
SiteShrimp supports project-specific requirements through a flexible schema.

Teams can upload and use:
• Contracts and employer's requirements
• Internal QA/QC programmes
• Industry standards (e.g. FIDIC, SIA, REDAS, or bespoke developer terms)

The Requirements Advisor cross-checks defect records against these references, helping identify compliance gaps across the project.

Bundled reference samples (e.g. CONQUAS, Quality Mark, Good Industry Practice guides, PSSCOC, HDB checklists) are included as illustrative starting points. The same structure can be extended across jurisdictions or organisations by swapping the reference data.
about.different_body:
AI operates at the moment of capture — photo to structured record in a single step — rather than as a back-office reporting layer.

Prompts can be tuned to match regulatory or contractual language so outputs align directly with how teams report on site.

Users retain control:
• Choose AI provider (cloud or local)
• Pause or disable AI at any time
• Track usage with a call counter
• Re-analyse existing records when prompts improve

The Requirements Advisor extends this further by evaluating the full defect set against project-specific references, surfacing gaps in plain language.
about.audience_body:
• Developers, contractors, and subcontractors managing defects, progress, and QA across projects

• Facilities managers and building owners handling inspections, DLP, and maintenance records

• Renovation and interior teams managing snag lists and handovers

• Consultants, QPs, and assessors recording inspections and sign-offs with traceable evidence

• SMEs and solo users needing a free, multilingual, and deployable solution (including self-host options)
